overall_summary: Deduplicated performance analysis shows clear audience preference for high-concept astronomy, weird planetary physics ('What If' / extreme worlds), and bizarre evolutionary biology ('Sharks vs. Trees/Saturn'). Space anomaly and extreme planetary environments dominate the highest view counts and engagement ratios, specifically videos involving exotic matter, extreme weather on other planets, and counter-intuitive cosmic comparisons.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) outperform standard fact formats by framing cosmic realities as experiential threats.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' immersion mechanics focused on extreme, visually distinct exoplanets.

winning_patterns.evidence: Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year (981 views) and shark/age comparisons generate high engagement relative to their age.
winning_patterns.action: Pair familiar biological entities or everyday objects against extreme cosmic timescales or scales.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract Psychological Trivia & Minor Brain Hacks
weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on songs stuck in your head (e.g., Jc04LVKNd2s with 17 views, ef3ND4qiRHc with 71 views) show significantly lower velocity than physical/cosmic anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize micro-psychology tricks unless tied to dark, high-stakes neurological anomalies.
